concepts.name: What GPS is
concepts.source_span: GPS stands for Global Positioning System.

questions.stem: What does GPS stand for?
Which country built and runs GPS?
Does a GPS receiver send signals to the satellites?
How does a phone work out where it is with GPS?
options: By listening to radio signals from satellites

questions.stem: What does a GPS satellite broadcast?
options: Its position and the exact time the signal was sent

concepts.name: The satellites
concepts.source_span: The satellites orbit about 20,200 kilometres above the Earth.

questions.stem: At about what height do GPS satellites orbit?
How many orbital planes does the GPS constellation have?
About how often does a GPS satellite circle the Earth?
What do GPS satellites carry for accurate timing?
What is the minimum size of the GPS constellation?

concepts.name: Measuring distance with time
concepts.source_span: Distance equals the speed of light multiplied by the travel time.

questions.stem: How is the distance to a satellite calculated?
options: Speed of light multiplied by the travel time
Height of the satellite divided by 2
Time divided by the speed of light
Speed of sound divided by time

questions.stem: At what speed do radio signals travel?
options: The speed of the satellite only

questions.stem: About how long does a GPS signal take to reach the ground?
What does the receiver compare to find the travel time?
options: The arrival time and the time the signal was sent

questions.stem: Why does accurate timing matter so much for GPS?
options: Light travels so fast that tiny time errors become big distance errors
Phones need to know the date

concepts.name: Trilateration
concepts.source_span: Trilateration finds a position from its distances to several known points.

questions.stem: What does trilateration find?
options: A position from distances to several known points

questions.stem: The distance to one satellite places the receiver on:
options: A straight line to the Earth

questions.stem: Two satellites narrow the position down to:
options: A circle where two spheres meet

questions.stem: Three satellites narrow the position down to:
options: A single point on the ground every time
Two points, one usually far out in space

questions.stem: Which method does GPS use to find a position?

concepts.name: Why four satellites are needed
concepts.source_span: A fourth satellite lets the receiver solve for its own clock error as well as its three position coordinates.

questions.stem: Why is a fourth satellite needed?
options: To solve for the receiver's own clock error

questions.stem: Why is the receiver's clock a problem?
options: It is cheaper and less accurate than an atomic clock
It is too fast to read

questions.stem: What does a small clock error turn into?
How many satellite signals does a receiver need at least?
Besides the clock error, what does the receiver solve for?

concepts.name: Relativity and corrections
concepts.source_span: The net effect of their speed and weaker gravity is that the satellite clocks run faster by about 38 microseconds per day compared with clocks on the ground.

questions.stem: Which theory affects the satellite clocks?
By about how much do the satellite clocks run faster each day?
What would happen to GPS positions without the correction?
options: They would drift by several kilometres each day
They would be wrong only at night

questions.stem: How is the relativity effect handled?
options: The satellite clocks are adjusted so the correction is built in
